## Exam Module C Dec 18 - Q1(a) fraud risk
# Exam Module C: Dec 18 - Q1(a) fraud risk
[[Exam Module C: Dec 18 - case]]
(a) Identify any fraud risk which would cause material misstatements of ELL’s purchase and trade payable process. (2 marks)
---- 
- Understate the liability - as requirement of credit ratio
- Internal control - segregation of duty - 
	- fictitious payments record and cheque payments to himself - [[misappropriation of assets]]
	- Management - inform to do so is easier

[[fraud risk factors]]
---- 
## Solution
ELL may wish to understate its trade payables and purchases in order to improve its ~liquidity position~, in particular, ELL is subject to meet the current ratio of greater than 1 as set out in the loan agreement.

In addition, the same trade payable clerk is responsible for recording purchases and trade payables and processing payments, fraud risk on ~misappropriation of funds~ by the trade payable clerk would increase because he can create fictitious purchases and process fake payments by himself.

# QP/Practice/Audit/fraud

## Exam Module C Dec 18 - Q1(b) control risk
# Exam Module C: Dec 18 - Q1(b) control risk
[[Exam Module C: Dec 18 - case]]
(b) Evaluate the control risk of material misstatements in ELL’s purchase and trade payable process. (3 marks)
[[control risk]]

---- 
1. Segregation of duty
2. Lost a few key accounting staff - lack of people 
---- 
## Solution
The audit team should concern whether the purchases and trade payables are **accurately** and **completely** recorded.

The audit team noted that ELL ~lost a few key accounting staff~ and vacant positions have not been filled. This indicated a **lack of segregation of duties** which would affect the effectiveness of ELL’s internal control.

Accordingly, the control risk of material misstatements of ELL’s purchase and trade payable process is considered to be high.

# QP/D/Audit/RA

## Exam Module C Dec 18 - Q1(c) RoMM - accuracy
# Exam Module C: Dec 18 - Q1(c) RoMM - accuracy
[[Exam Module C: Dec 18 - case]]
(c) Evaluate the risk of material misstatements of ELL’s subcontracting fees in terms of accuracy assertion. (5 marks)
---- 
Fixed, variable

Significant amount
Complex transaction - detailed labour cost and mark up

1. Fixed - machine rental
2. Variable - mark-up labour
---- 
## Solution
Subcontracting fee is a **significant component** of ELL’s production costs. The auditor ~should concern~ whether the subcontracting fees are accurately recorded in the financial statements.

The subcontracting fees are calculated based on a formula where some of the parameters, such as the labour cost mark-up and the fixed monthly fee, are predetermined in the subcontracting agreements. However, these predetermined parameters may vary among subcontractors. This **increases the complexity** of the subcontracting fees calculation.

Further, the subcontracting fee is calculated based on the actual direct labour costs incurred by the subcontractors where such **information is not maintained by ELL** itself. ELL is ~required to estimate an amount or obtain the actual amount~ from the subcontractors for the determination of the subcontracting fee.

Subcontracting is a **new arrangement** this year, therefore, the personnel who oversee the related financial reporting process may not be familiar with this new arrangement and its control may not be effective.

As such, the determination of subcontracting fees may require further reconciliation process before both parties agree a final subcontracting fee.

The overall internal control of ELL is considered to be **ineffective,** therefore, material misstatements on subcontracting fees may not be detected.

Based on the above consideration, the risk of material misstatements on the accuracy assertion of ELL’s subcontracting fees is considered to be high.

# QP/Practice/Audit/RA

## Exam Module C Dec 18 - Q1(d) substantive procedures - completeness AP
# Exam Module C: Dec 18 - Q1(d) substantive procedures - completeness AP
(d) Propose substantive procedures to audit the completeness of ELL’s trade payables at the year end date. (5 marks)
---- 
[[trade payables and accruals - audit procedures]]
[[AP - completeness procedures]]

- Trace a sample from PO, to invoice, transaction records and payment to ensure there is no missing
- Reconcile the AP listings and the ledger balance
- Reasonableness testing on the change of AP, AP turnover days
---- 
## Solution
The audit team should perform the following procedures to audit the completeness of ELL’s trade payables:
- Reconcile the listing of trade payables to the general ledger balance by casting and cross-casting.
- Examine **post year end purchase transactions** to identify if there are any unrecorded trade payables.
- Obtain **statements** from the overseas suppliers for LED chips and **trace** these back to ELL’s accounting records to identify if there are significant discrepancies.
- Obtain statements (if any) or written documentation from the **subcontractors** and **trace** these back to ELL’s records of the subcontracting fee payables to identify if there are significant discrepancies.
- Examine the ~subcontracting agreements~ for the terms of the subcontracting fees to ensure appropriate fees have been accrued for by ELL as trade payables.
- Send **confirmation** requests to the overseas suppliers of LED chips and subcontractors with ~material outstanding balances~ to confirm the year end balances due by ELL.
- Send **confirmation** requests to the ~key suppliers~ which have ~nil or small~ outstanding balances due by ELL at the year end date.
- Perform **comparison** of the current year balance for trade payables to the previous year to check for reasonableness.

# QP/Practice/Audit/specific/AP

# AP - completeness procedures
- From a [[listing of trade payables]] reconcile the total to the general ledger by casting and cross-casting.
- Consider whether there could be significant unrecorded liabilities by **inquiries** of management; examine post year-end transactions.
- Select a sample of suppliers' statements and **trace** these back to the supplier's accounts.
- Examine files of **unmatched** purchase orders and supplier invoices for any ~unrecorded liabilities~.
- Perform a **confirmation** of trade payables for a sample (see Section 6.2 for details of the trade payables' confirmation). [[confirmation of trade payables AP]]
	- significant
	- Nil or small - key suppliers
- Complete the **disclosure checklist** to ensure that all the disclosures relevant to liabilities have been made.
- Perform comparisons of the following data to check for **reasonableness**:
– Current year balances for trade payables and accruals to the previous year.
– The amounts owed to a sample of individual suppliers in the trade payables listing to amounts owed to these suppliers in the previous year.
– The payables' turnover and payables' days to the previous year and industry data.

---- 
* Examine post year-end purchase transactions to identify if there are any unrecorded trade payables
- Examine agreements fo the terms of the fees to ensure appropriate fees has been accrued by xxx as trade payable
# QP/D/Audit/specific/AP

# confirmation of trade payables AP
Confirmation of trade payables is not often used in practice because the auditor can test trade payables by examining reliable, independent evidence in the form of **suppliers' invoices and suppliers' statements**. However, it may be used where an entity's internal controls are weak, and suppliers' statements are available where other internal documentation is not. Confirmation of trade payables provides evidence primarily for the ~completeness~ assertion.

What confirmations will take place will depend on the auditor's **assessment of internal control**:

(a) Where the entity has **strong** internal controls and the auditor has reasonable assurance that all liabilities are recorded, the confirmation will focus primarily, if not entirely, on ~large balances~.

(b) Where the auditor **suspects** there may be unrecorded liabilities, ~regular suppliers~ who have small or zero balances on their accounts and a sample of other accounts will be confirmed in addition to any large balances.

Auditors use a **positive confirmation** (referred to as a blank or zero-balance confirmation). This means the confirmation does not state the amount owed but requires the supplier to provide a detailed statement of the account, including the balance owed at the period end. When the confirmation is received back, the amount must be ~reconciled~ with the entity's records.

# QP/D/Audit/specific/AP

# AP - existence procedures
- **Vouch** selected amounts from the trade payables listing and accruals schedule to supporting documentation (purchase orders and suppliers' invoices and so on).
- **Reconcile** a selection of suppliers' statements to the relevant suppliers' accounts.
- Perform a **confirmation** of trade payables for a sample.
- Perform **analytical procedures** which compare current period balances to the previous period to test reasonableness. Use ratios to calculate payables' turnover and compare the results to the previous year.

Similar to [[AP - completeness procedures]]
# QP/D/Audit/specific/AP

# AP - rights and obligations
**Vouch** a sample of balances to supporting documentation to obtain audit evidence on rights and obligations.

# QP/D/Audit/specific/AP

# AP - accuracy, valuation and allocation
- **Recalculate** the sample of suppliers' invoices to confirm the amounts due are correct.
- **Vouch** selected samples from the trade payables listing and accruals listing to the supporting documentation (purchase orders, minutes authorising expenditure and suppliers' invoices etc.).
- Select suppliers' statements and **reconcile** these to the relevant suppliers' accounts.
- For ~accruals~, **recalculate** the amount of the certain accrual to ensure the calculation is correct. 
- Perform the following **comparisons**:
	- The current period balances for trade payables and accruals to the previous period.
	- The amounts owed to a sample of individual suppliers in the trade payables listing to amounts owed to these suppliers in the previous year.
	- The payables' turnover and payables' days to the previous year and industry data.

# QP/D/Audit/specific/AP

# AP - cut-off
* For a sample, **compare the actual dates** with the dates they were recorded in the ledger to check cut-off has been applied correctly.
* **Test transactions** either side of the period end to determine whether amounts have been correctly recognised.
* Perform **analytical procedures** on purchase returns, by comparing the purchase returns as a percentage of sales or cost of sales to the previous year.

# QP/D/Audit/specific/AP

# AP - occurrence
For a sample of vouchers, **inspect** ~supporting documentation~ such as authorised purchase orders.

# QP/D/Audit/specific/AP

# AP - classification
**Review** the trade payables listing to identify any ~large debits~ (which should be reclassified as receivables or deposits) or ~long-term liabilities~ which should be disclosed separately.

# QP/D/Audit/specific/AP

# AP - presentation
**Read** the ~disclosure notes~ to ensure the information is accurate and properly presented at the appropriate amounts.

# QP/D/Audit/specific/AP

## Exam Module C Dec 18 - Q2(a) during inventory count
# Exam Module C: Dec 18 - Q2(a) during inventory count
(a) Propose procedures that the audit team should perform during the observation of ELL’s inventory count on 31 December 2018. (5 marks)
---- 
[[physical inventory count]] [[attendance at inventory count]]
- Follow instruction
- Test count - two-way - management records vs physical count
	- focus on high value items - LED chip
- Procedure to identify obsolete, ... LED chip
- Inventory 3rd party held - subcontractors, separately identified

---- 
## Solution
The audit team should perform the following procedures during the inventory count:
- Observe whether ELL’s staff are **following instructions** as this will help to ensure the count is complete and accurate.
- Observe whether all the movements and production processes are **suspended** so that there are no movement of the stock items during the inventory count.
- Ensure **procedures to identify damaged**, obsolete and slow moving inventory are executed.
- Obtain ~information on the inventories’ age~, condition and usage, and in case of work-in-progress, its stage of completion to ensure that it is later valued properly.
- Obtain the **last serial numbers** of the goods received and dispatched for the upcoming ~cut-off test~ at the final audit.
- **Conclude** whether the inventory count is properly carried out and is sufficiently reliable as a basis of determining the existence of the inventories. For example, whether the inventories ~held on behalf of third parties~ are separated, whether discrepancies were found during the test count.
- Gain an **overall impression** of the ~levels and values of inventories~ held so that the auditor may, in due course, judge whether the figure of inventory appearing in the financial statements is reasonable.

# QP/Practice/Audit/specific/inventory

# test counts
When carrying out **test counts** the auditors should **select items** from the ~management's count records~ and from the ~physical inventory~ and check one to the other, to confirm the accuracy of the count records. These ~two-way tests~ provide evidence for **completeness** and **existence**. The auditors should concentrate on **high value** inventory. If the results of the test counts are not satisfactory, the auditors may request that inventory is recounted.

# QP/D/Audit/specific/inventory

## Exam Module C Dec 18 - Q2(c) 3rd party inventory
# Exam Module C: Dec 18 - Q2(c) 3rd party inventory
Other than the inventories which were kept in the ELL’s warehouse and factory premises, identify any other inventories that ELL had recorded at the year end date. Given the fact that no inventory count for these inventories was arranged by ELL, advise measures or procedures that the audit team could perform in order to obtain reliable evidence to confirm their existence. (7 marks)
---- 
[[physical inventory count]] [[Inventory held by third party]]
---- 
## Solution
Other inventories that ELL had recorded at the year end date included inventories ~held by the subcontractors~ and ~goods-in-transit~.

For inventories held by the subcontractors, if **material**, the audit team can perform the following procedures subsequent to the reporting date to confirm their **existence**:
- Obtain ~direct confirmations~ from the subcontractors to confirm the quantities and ownership of the inventories held by them on ELL’s behalf.
- ~Inspect any documentation~ regarding the goods held by the subcontractors.
- If possible, request ELL or subcontractors to perform an ~inventory count~ and such count will be attended by the auditor.
- Assess the ~effectiveness of the control~ implemented by the subcontractors regarding their inventory count procedures.
- Perform ~roll-backward procedures~ to **reconcile** these inventories at the year end date.

For **goods-in-transit**, if ~material~, the audit team can perform the following procedures:
- Obtain the ~shipping or other delivery evidence~ to verify the existence of the goods in transit.
- Examine the **evidence** of the ~subsequent goods received~.

## Exam Module C Dec 18 - Q3(a),(b) bank loan and finance lease payables
# Exam Module C: Dec 18 - Q3(a),(b) bank loan and finance lease payables
Q3. ELL had recorded a bank loan and finance lease payables in its 2018 financial statements. Both the bank loan and finance lease payables were classified and presented as non-current liabilities, with a current portion of finance lease payables being classified as current liabilities. The principal of the bank loan is repayable by 2023 and interest is repayable on a bi-annual basis. The finance leases are repayable by monthly instalments until 2022.
---- 
**(a)** Propose procedures to audit the classification and presentation assertions of (i) bank loan and (ii) finance lease payables. (5 marks)
[[Specific audit procedures]] [[non-current liabilities - audit procedures]] [[classification and presentation]]
**(b)** Propose procedures to audit the accuracy and completeness assertions of interest expenses recorded by ELL relating to its (i) bank loan and (ii) finance leases.
---- 
(i) bank loan
- Review agreement with bank
- Ascertain the bank loan period
- Ensure the condition of liquidity ratio is not exceeded


(ii) finance lease payables
- Operating lease or finance lease? Review agreement with lessor

---- 
## Solution
(a) The audit team should perform the following procedures to audit the **classification and presentation** assertions of ELL’s bank loan and finance lease payables:

(i) Bank loan
- Examine the **bank loan agreement** to confirm the repayment of the loan is repayable ~beyond 12 months~ from the reporting date.
- As the loan agreement stipulates conditions with which ELL **must comply a current ratio** of greater than 1, the audit team should obtain evidence to ~confirm whether ELL has complied~ to such conditions. Otherwise, a demand of the immediate repayment of the loan would trigger the reclassification of such a loan from non-current to current liabilities.
- Obtain **direct confirmation** from the respective bank to confirm the ~due date~ for the repayment of the loan.

ii) Finance lease payables
- Examine the **respective agreement(s)** to confirm the ~repayment schedules~ of all finance lease payables.
- **Recalculate** the ~current portion~ of the finance lease payables.
- Examine the terms of respective agreement(s) to confirm the arrangements ~satisfied the definition of finance leases~ in accordance with the relevant **accounting standards**.
---- 
The audit team should perform the following procedures to audit the **accuracy and completeness** assertions of interest expenses of the bank loan and finance leases:

(i) Bank loan
- As the **interest** is payable on a bi-annual basis, **examine** the ~two interest **payments**~ to the **bank advices** to confirm the amount of interest expenses to ensure it is accurately recorded.
- Examine the bank statements to **trace** the amount of interest expenses recorded by ELL to ensure the completeness.
- **Recalculate the** interest expense by applying the market (or agreed) interest rate on the principal loan balance and assess if there are significant discrepancies when comparing the recorded interest expenses.
- Examine the **subsequent interest payment** to ensure no significant unrecorded interest.

(ii) Finance leases
- Examine the finance lease **repayment schedules**, aggregate the total interests for the year and compare to the recorded interest expenses.
- **Compare** the current year interest expenses to that of the prior year and ensure if the changes are reasonable.
- Check the monthly **bank statements** and agree the portion of interest expenses paid and aggregate repayments of principal.
- Examine the ~annual statement sent by the lenders~ which may state the annual interest payment for the respective financial lease arrangements, and compare such annual interests to the recorded interest expenses.
